svg.title: Friction supplies the centripetal force
svg.desc: Top: a car on a curve of large radius r with velocity v tangent to the path; friction f points toward the center. Bottom: on a curve of smaller radius r′ at the same speed v, the centripetal force Fc must be larger. Since Fc = mac, f = Fc is parallel to ac. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Friction points to the center of a flat curve
Green: velocity, tangent to the path. Purple: static friction, the centripetal force. At the same
speed, a tighter curve needs more of it.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
